# k0rdent_instance_group (Resource)

A group of bare hosts provisioned from a ClusterType's node pools, without a Kubernetes control plane.

Requires `region` and `project`, on the provider block or on this resource.

**What replaces it.** Changing `cluster_type`, `id`, `node_pool`, `project`, `region` or `ssh_access` cannot be done in place and replaces the instance group. An instance group's hosts run tenant workloads, and a replacement deprovisions every host in it before new ones are provisioned. So a plan that would replace it fails and names the attribute, unless `allow_replace = true` is set on the resource. Everything else changes in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "k0rdent_cluster_type" "gpu" {
  id = "gpu-training"
}

resource "k0rdent_instance_group" "hosts" {
  id           = "training-01-hosts"
  cluster_type = data.k0rdent_cluster_type.gpu.self_link
  display_name = "Training hosts"

  node_pool = {
    gpu-workers = {
      size = 4
    }
  }

  # Set when hosts are built. Changing it replaces the group, which
  # needs `allow_replace = true`.
  ssh_access = [
    {
      username        = "ops"
      ssh_public_keys = [trimspace(file("~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub"))]
      sudo            = "ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL"
    },
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_type` (String) Reference to the ClusterType version whose node pools describe the hardware to provision. The `/versions/{id}` segment is optional. See `cluster_type_resolved`, and the note on the `kubernetes_cluster` resource's equivalent attribute. **Known gap.** A tenant can't read the hardware or the image behind a ClusterType's machine types, so choosing a ClusterType for its hardware means writing one an operator named. The [hardcoded values](../guides/hardcoded-values.md) guide names the side that has to change. **Can force replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`): replaced only when the new reference names a different ClusterType binding, not merely a different spelling of the same one.
- `id` (String) Instance group name, the one the platform shows, and the id this resource is imported by. Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter. Required, so that a plan can read it before creating it: a create that stopped waiting leaves it still being built, and the plan that would replace it is refused with the way to wait for it instead. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL. String length must be at most 63.

### Optional

- `allow_replace` (Boolean) Permit a plan that replaces this instance group. Left out or `false`, a change that cannot be made in place fails the plan, naming the attribute that forces the replacement, instead of destroying the instance group and creating another. Set it to `true` in the same configuration as the change to let the replacement go ahead, and remove it afterwards to put the guard back. It is read from the configuration being planned and must be known at plan time. It is never sent to the platform: setting or removing it on its own is an update that changes nothing there.
- `description` (String) Free-form description. The other mutable field.
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name. One of only two mutable fields on this resource.
- `node_pool` (Attributes Map) Host counts per pool, keyed by the ClusterType node pool's id.

Unlike a cluster's `node_pool` this is not sparse: the platform provisions exactly the pools named here. Growing a pool scales in place. **Shrinking a pool, or adding or removing one, replaces the whole group**, because the API implements scale up only and rejects everything else on this field with `409 CONFLICT_IMMUTABLE`.

A scale waits, within the `update` timeout, while another operation on the group finishes or its quota accounting settles. A pool whose desired size disagrees with the hosts it holds cannot be scaled until that is corrected, and a plan that grows one warns before the apply fails. **Known gap.** A pool's machine type is readable only as a name, not as hardware, so choosing a pool for its hardware means writing its id as a literal. The [hardcoded values](../guides/hardcoded-values.md) guide names the side that has to change. **Can force replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`): replaced when a pool shrinks, or when pools are added or removed. **Constraints:** Must name at least one pool. Each pool id must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, not ending with a hyphen, and at most 63 characters long. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node_pool))
- `project` (String) Project this resource belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project`. It's part of the resource's API path, so a resource can't move between projects. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `region` (String) Region this resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `region`. It's part of the resource's API path, so a resource can't move between regions. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `ssh_access` (Attributes Set) Linux users written onto every host in the group when it is provisioned, each with the public keys allowed to log in as that user. Up to 32 users. Only public keys go here. The contract says the platform never stores or generates a private key.

Set it. A group with no SSH keys can fail with `INVALID_CONFIGURATION`.

**Changing it replaces the whole group**, unless it's left out or empty and the platform already reports no users. The platform returns the users sorted by username, so the order they are written in here makes no difference. **Can force replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`): replaced when it changes, unless the platform already reports none and none is configured. **Constraints:** Set must contain at most 32 elements. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ssh_access))
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) How long each operation may take before it fails. Left out, `create` and `delete` default to `3h` and every other operation to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `cluster_type_resolved` (String) The `clusterType` value the platform returned, verbatim. It can be a relative path or an absolute URI, so it can differ in form from `cluster_type` while naming the same version.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this instance group.
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state as last read from the platform.
- `vpc` (String) Id of the VPC this instance group brought with it. Name the VPC through this rather than a data source: it stays known while the instance group changes, so a peering or a security-group binding that names it is not replaced. A peering takes it as `vpc`, and a peering in this project that points at it takes it as `remote_vpc`.

<a id="nestedatt--node_pool"></a>
### Nested Schema for `node_pool`

Required:

- `size` (Number) Number of hosts to provision in this pool. **Constraints:** Value must be between 0 and 2147483647.


<a id="nestedatt--ssh_access"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ssh_access`

Required:

- `ssh_public_keys` (List of String) Public keys, each one `authorized_keys` line, allowed to log in as this user. From 1 to 32. The platform accepts `ssh-ed25519`, `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256/384/521`, `ssh-rsa` of at least 2048 bits, and the `sk-` security-key variants. Kept in the order written. A key must not start or end with whitespace, since the platform trims it: read one from a file with `trimspace(file(...))`, because `file()` keeps the trailing newline. **Constraints:** Must hold from 1 to 32 keys. Each key must be one line with no whitespace at either end, and at most 16384 characters long. Read one from a file with `trimspace(file(...))`.
- `username` (String) Linux username to provision on every host. Must match `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`. **Constraints:** Must start with a lowercase letter or an underscore, then up to 31 lowercase letters, digits, underscores or hyphens.

Optional:

- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name for this entry. **Constraints:** String length must be at most 255.
- `sudo` (String) A sudo fragment granting this user privileges, such as `ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL`. **Constraints:** String length must be at most 4096.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Bounds the whole create, including the wait until the platform reports it ready. Left out, it defaults to `3h`, or to the provider's `operation_timeout` once the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. **Constraints:** Must be a positive duration of hours, minutes or seconds, such as `45m`, `2h` or `1h30m`.
- `delete` (String) Bounds the whole destroy, including the wait until the platform reports it gone. Left out, it defaults to `3h`, or to the provider's `operation_timeout` once the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. **Constraints:** Must be a positive duration of hours, minutes or seconds, such as `45m`, `2h` or `1h30m`.
- `update` (String) Bounds the whole update, including the wait until the platform settles. Left out, it defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. **Constraints:** Must be a positive duration of hours, minutes or seconds, such as `45m`, `2h` or `1h30m`.

## Timeouts

The `timeouts` block sets how long each operation may take before it fails:

- `create` (default `3h`). Bounds the whole create, including the wait until the platform reports it ready.
- `update` (default `2h`). Bounds the whole update, including the wait until the platform settles.
- `delete` (default `3h`). Bounds the whole destroy, including the wait until the platform reports it gone.

A create or a delete builds or frees hardware, which can take more than 2 hours, so it defaults to `3h`. Every other default is the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. Once it's set, it's every operation's default, these two included. A value of zero or less is refused at plan time rather than read as no limit.

A wait that runs out, or a run that is interrupted, stops nothing on the platform. A create that stops waiting fails, and Terraform taints the object: run `terraform untaint` on it and then `terraform apply`, which waits for the same object. A delete that stops waiting fails and stays in state, and the next `terraform destroy` waits for the same delete without sending another.

```terraform
resource "k0rdent_instance_group" "example" {
  # ...

  timeouts {
    create = "45m"
    update = "45m"
    delete = "45m"
  }
}
```

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# The same address with each part named. Leave out region and project to
# use the provider's.
import {
  to = k0rdent_instance_group.example
  identity = {
    region  = "us-texas-1"
    project = "cp-production"
    id      = "my-hosts"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The resource's id.

#### Optional

- `project` (String) Project the resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `project` on import.
- `region` (String) Region the resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `region` on import.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Takes every id form `terraform import` does. The first command below uses
# the provider's region and project, the second names them. If you name them,
# set both in the resource block too, or the next plan replaces the group.
import {
  to = k0rdent_instance_group.example
  id = "us-texas-1/cp-production/my-hosts"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import k0rdent_instance_group.example my-hosts

terraform import k0rdent_instance_group.example us-texas-1/cp-production/my-hosts
```
